items.abstract: <jats:p>Log anomaly detection is critical for ensuring the reliability of large-scale distributed systems. Existing methods often fail to balance adaptability to concept drift with the interpretability required for effective root cause analysis. Deep learning models generally lack transparency, while Large Language Model (LLM)-based approaches are prone to hallucination and exhibit high latency. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a neuro-symbolic framework, PGCLR+SESAM, which combines two complementary modules for robust log analysis. The first module, Prompt-Guided Causal Log Reasoning (PGCLR), uses an LLM (LLaMA-3.3-70B) and prompt-based causal reconstruction to infer multi-hop dependencies among log events and generate explicit root-cause reasoning chains. The second module, Self-Evolving Semantic Anomaly Memory (SESAM), implements an active memory-guided prompting mechanism. In contrast to passive storage, SESAM dynamically retrieves and injects semantic summaries of long-tail anomalies to refine the reasoning context and enhance generalisation under distribution drift. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets, LogHub~2.0 (15M entries) and LogLAB (9M entries), demonstrate that this approach outperforms previous methods, including specialized LLMs such as LLM-LADE, achieving an F1-score of 0.961, maintaining real-time inference efficiency with less than 150 ms per sequence. Automated interpretability metrics, including Graph Edit Distance and Semantic Consistency Score, as well as human evaluation, are used to quantitatively assess the structural accuracy of the generated explanations. The findings demonstrate that the proposed framework enables transparent causal reasoning and offers a practical solution for trustworthy, self-adaptive system reliability management.</jats:p>
title: Prompt-Guided Causal Log Reasoning with Self-Evolving Semantic Memory for Robust Anomaly Detection in Noisy Distributed Systems

items.abstract: <jats:p>Oxygen lance control is a critical decision-making task in basic oxygen furnace (BOF) steelmaking. It regulates lance height to control decarburization rate, aiming to achieve stability. Existing approaches either rely on human expertise, requiring long-term training and experience accumulation, or use traditional machine-learning models that simplify the problem into numerical regression, resulting in limited interpretability and adaptability. In this work, we are the first to reformulate oxygen lance control as a structured multimodal generative decision-making task and propose a self-evolving reasoning Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) agent that performs structured reasoning. The agent jointly perceives real-time furnace mouth flame videos and historical process data to generate structured decision paths. To address the scarcity of high-quality annotated industrial data, we introduce OT-SERA, an Operation‐Trajectory guided Self‐Evolving Reasoning MLLM Agent for structured decision-making. OT-SERA includes an initialization phase and a refinement phase. In the Operation-Trajectory Guided Reasoning Initialization (OTGRI) phase: operation trajectories from real BOF steelmaking guide the generation of structured chain-of-thoughts (CoTs), which are then used to warm-up the agent by fine-tuning. In the Self-Evolving Reasoning Refinement (SERR) phase: the agent improves reasoning paths through self-evolving updates with path backtracking, automatically constructing high-quality CoTs without additional human annotation. Repeated the SERR further improve CoTs quality, highlighting the effectiveness. Extensive experiments on real-world BOF data show that OT-SERA outperforms strong time series and multimodal baselines under both normal and hard operating conditions. By integrating multimodal perception, OTGRI, and SERR, this work provides an effective solution for intelligent control of complex industrial processes.</jats:p>
title: An Operation‐Trajectory Guided Self-Evolving Reasoning Multimodal LLM Agent for Oxygen Lance Control in BOF Steelmaking

items.abstract: <jats:p>Securing the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) is paramount, yet proprietary protocols remain vulnerable to deep-state logic flaws that traditional fuzzers often fail to reach. We propose MALF, a Multi-Agent LLM Fuzzing Framework that couples a dynamic Industrial Security Knowledge Graph (ISKG) with collaborative cognitive agents for effective, efficient, and trustworthy IIoT security testing. A self-evolving knowledge loop mitigates LLM hallucinations by grounding the generation in verifiable graph constraints; QLoRA-tuned models aligned with hexadecimal features enable low-latency mutation; and Chain-of-Thought reasoning reconstructs protocol states for intent-driven attacks. On a heterogeneous testbed spanning five industrial protocols and ten vendors, MALF achieves an average Test Case Acceptance Rate of 88.3% (peak 91.2% on Modbus/TCP) and 91.2% ISKG-defined state coverage, outperforming rule-based, RL-based, and LLM baselines. On a 15-vulnerability N-Day benchmark, MALF detects all known cases, against 60%, 47%, 40%, and 27% for NCMFuzzer, MARLFuzz, BooFuzz, and Fuzz4All, respectively. In a separate real-world campaign, MALF further identifies 14 previously unknown vulnerability candidates, of which four have been assigned CNVD identifiers (CNVD-2024-16009, CNVD-2025-22875, CNVD-2025-29811, CNVD-2026-06041) and 10 remain under vendor review. These results provide controlled-testbed evidence that knowledge-grounded AI agents can systematically expose deep-state vulnerabilities in opaque IIoT environments.</jats:p>
title: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Fuzzing for Industrial IoT with Knowledge-Driven Cognitive Reasoning
